exposure: direct visualization of adjacent tissues invasion
Method A (at least one abnormal MRI sign)
Method B (at least two abnormal MRI signs)
Method C (combined presence of intraplacental dark bands and focal interruption of myometrial border)
outcome: Placental Adhesion Disorders (PAD) confirmed by histological findings
cohort: Sixty-one patients with placenta previa and ultrasound suspicion of placental adhesion disorders (PAD) who underwent abdomino-pelvic MRI.
finding: MRI is a useful imaging technique to assess PAD in patients with placenta previa, with Method B (the presence of at least two abnormal MRI signs) being the most accurate criterion to identify PAD.
